**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 54, verses 47–49:**

Allah's statement: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and insanity﴾. There are four issues in this.

**The first issue:** Allah's statement ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and insanity﴾ means they are in deviation from the truth. (سُعُرٍ) means burning. It is also said that it means madness, as was mentioned earlier in this surah.

(*On the day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces: "Taste the touch of Saqar."*) In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about qadar (divine decree), and then this was revealed: (*On the day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces: "Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, We created all things according to a measure."*). It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, who said: a hasan sahih hadith. Muslim also related from Tawus, who said: I met people from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who used to say: "Everything is by qadar." He said: And I heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Everything is by qadar, even incapacity and shrewdness" — or "shrewdness and incapacity." This is a refutation of the doctrine of the Qadariyya (the deniers of qadar).

(*Taste*) means: it is said to them, "Taste." Its "touch" is the pain they experience upon falling into it. (*Saqar*) is one of the names of Hell and is not declined, because it is a feminine proper noun; likewise Laza and Jahannam. Ata said: Saqar is the sixth level of Hell. Qutrub said: Saqar derives from saqarathu al-shams and sadhdharathu, meaning the sun scorched and blackened him. A day described as musmaqir or musmaqqir means one of intense heat.

**The second issue:** Allah's statement ﴿Indeed, all things﴾: the common reading is (كُلَّ) in the accusative. Abu al-Sammal read (كُلُّ) in the nominative, as a subject of inception (mubtada'). Whoever reads it in the accusative does so by supposing an implied verb, and this is the choice of the Kufans, because (إِنَّ) requires a verb and so the accusative is more appropriate to it. The accusative is also more explicit in indicating the generality of created things belonging to Allah the Exalted, because if you omitted the explanatory (خَلَقْناهُ, "We created it") and made the first word prominent, it would become (إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ بِقَدَرٍ). It is not valid for (خَلَقْناهُ) to be an attributive description of (شَيْءٍ), because an attribute does not operate upon what precedes the thing described, and it cannot be an explanation of something that governs what comes before it.

**The third issue:** What the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna) hold is that Allah, glorified is He, decreed things, meaning He knew their measures, their states, and their times before bringing them into existence. Then He brought into existence those things that had been foreknown in His knowledge, in the manner that had been foreknown. Thus no event occurs in the higher or lower world except that it proceeds from His knowledge, power, and will, not from His creation. The creatures have in these matters only a kind of acquisition (iktisab), effort, attribution, and ascription. All of this arises for them only through the facilitation of Allah the Exalted, His power, His granting of success, and His inspiration, glorified is He; there is no god but Him, and there is no creator other than Him, as the Qur'an and the Sunna explicitly state. This is not as the Qadariyya and others say, that actions are up to us and terms of life are in the hand of others.

Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The delegation of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Actions are up to us, and terms of life are in the hand of others." Then these verses were revealed, up to His statement: (*Indeed, We created all things according to a measure*). They said: "O Muhammad, will He record sin against us and punish us?" He said: "You are the adversaries of Allah on the Day of Resurrection."

**The fourth issue:** Abu al-Zubayr related from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Magians of this nation are those who deny the decrees of Allah. If they fall ill, do not visit them; if they die, do not attend their funerals; and if you meet them, do not greet them with salam." Ibn Majah recorded it in his Sunan. He also recorded from Ibn Abbas and Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There are two categories of my nation who have no share in Islam: the people of irja' (postponement) and the people of qadar."

Al-Nahhas narrated with a chain: Ibrahim ibn Sharik al-Kufi related to us, saying: Uqba ibn Mukram al-Dabbi related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from Sa'id ibn Maysara, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Qadariyya are those who say that good and evil are in our hands; they have no share in my intercession, nor am I of them, nor are they of me."

In Sahih Muslim, it is recorded that Ibn Umar disassociated himself from them, and one does not disassociate oneself except from a disbeliever. Then he emphasized this by saying: "By Him by whom Abdullah ibn Umar swears, if any one of them had gold equal to Mount Uhud and spent it, Allah would not accept it from him until he believes in qadar." This is like His statement concerning the hypocrites: (*Nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger*). [See vol. 8, p. 163.] This is clear.

Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Belief in qadar removes anxiety and sorrow."

(*On the day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces: "Taste the touch of Saqar."*) In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about qadar (divine decree), and then this was revealed: (*On the day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces: "Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, We created all things according to a measure."*). It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, who said: a hasan sahih hadith. Muslim also related from Tawus, who said: I met people from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who used to say: "Everything is by qadar." He said: And I heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Everything is by qadar, even incapacity and shrewdness" — or "shrewdness and incapacity." This is a refutation of the doctrine of the Qadariyya (the deniers of qadar).

(*Taste*) means: it is said to them, "Taste." Its "touch" is the pain they experience upon falling into it. (*Saqar*) is one of the names of Hell and is not declined, because it is a feminine proper noun; likewise Laza and Jahannam. Ata said: Saqar is the sixth level of Hell. Qutrub said: Saqar derives from saqarathu al-shams and sadhdharathu, meaning the sun scorched and blackened him. A day described as musmaqir or musmaqqir means one of intense heat.

**The second issue:** Allah's statement ﴿Indeed, all things﴾: the common reading is (كُلَّ) in the accusative. Abu al-Sammal read (كُلُّ) in the nominative, as a subject of inception (mubtada'). Whoever reads it in the accusative does so by supposing an implied verb, and this is the choice of the Kufans, because (إِنَّ) requires a verb and so the accusative is more appropriate to it. The accusative is also more explicit in indicating the generality of created things belonging to Allah the Exalted, because if you omitted the explanatory (خَلَقْناهُ, "We created it") and made the first word prominent, it would become (إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ بِقَدَرٍ). It is not valid for (خَلَقْناهُ) to be an attributive description of (شَيْءٍ), because an attribute does not operate upon what precedes the thing described, and it cannot be an explanation of something that governs what comes before it.

**The third issue:** What the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna) hold is that Allah, glorified is He, decreed things, meaning He knew their measures, their states, and their times before bringing them into existence. Then He brought into existence those things that had been foreknown in His knowledge, in the manner that had been foreknown. Thus no event occurs in the higher or lower world except that it proceeds from His knowledge, power, and will, not from His creation. The creatures have in these matters only a kind of acquisition (iktisab), effort, attribution, and ascription. All of this arises for them only through the facilitation of Allah the Exalted, His power, His granting of success, and His inspiration, glorified is He; there is no god but Him, and there is no creator other than Him, as the Qur'an and the Sunna explicitly state. This is not as the Qadariyya and others say, that actions are up to us and terms of life are in the hand of others.

Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The delegation of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Actions are up to us, and terms of life are in the hand of others." Then these verses were revealed, up to His statement: (*Indeed, We created all things according to a measure*). They said: "O Muhammad, will He record sin against us and punish us?" He said: "You are the adversaries of Allah on the Day of Resurrection."

**The fourth issue:** Abu al-Zubayr related from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Magians of this nation are those who deny the decrees of Allah. If they fall ill, do not visit them; if they die, do not attend their funerals; and if you meet them, do not greet them with salam." Ibn Majah recorded it in his Sunan. He also recorded from Ibn Abbas and Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There are two categories of my nation who have no share in Islam: the people of irja' (postponement) and the people of qadar."

Al-Nahhas narrated with a chain: Ibrahim ibn Sharik al-Kufi related to us, saying: Uqba ibn Mukram al-Dabbi related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from Sa'id ibn Maysara, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Qadariyya are those who say that good and evil are in our hands; they have no share in my intercession, nor am I of them, nor are they of me."

In Sahih Muslim, it is recorded that Ibn Umar disassociated himself from them, and one does not disassociate oneself except from a disbeliever. Then he emphasized this by saying: "By Him by whom Abdullah ibn Umar swears, if any one of them had gold equal to Mount Uhud and spent it, Allah would not accept it from him until he believes in qadar." This is like His statement concerning the hypocrites: (*Nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger*). [See vol. 8, p. 163.] This is clear.

Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Belief in qadar removes anxiety and sorrow."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 50–55:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Our command is but one [word], like a glance of the eye.﴾ That is, but a single time, once.

(Like a glance of the eye) That is, My decree concerning My creation is swifter than the glance of the eye. Al-lamh (the glance) is looking quickly. It is said: he glanced at the lightning with his eye (lamaha al-barq bi-basarihi). In al-Sihah (the lexicon of al-Jawhari): lamaha and alamaha mean he saw it with a light look, and the noun is al-lamhah. Lamaha al-barq and al-najm lamhan means it flashed.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed We have destroyed your likes﴾ That is, your counterparts in disbelief from the previous nations. It is also said: your followers and your helpers.

(Then is there any who will remember?) That is, who will take heed. That is, everything the nations before them did, whether good or bad, was written against them. This explains His saying: (Indeed, We have created everything according to a measure).

(In the scriptures) That is, in the Preserved Tablet. It is said: in the records of the angels who record deeds. It is also said: in the Mother of the Book.

(And every small and great matter is recorded) That is, every sin, great or small, is written against its doer before he does it, so that he may be recompensed for it; and it is written once he has done it. Satara yasturu satran means he wrote; and istatara is similar to it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers﴾ Having described the disbelievers, He also described the believers.

(And rivers) meaning rivers of water, wine, honey and milk; this was said by Ibn Jurayj. It is in the singular because it is the end of the verse; and the singular may also indicate the plural. It is also said: in (nahr) there is the meaning of light and expanse; and from this comes al-nahar (the day), for its light. And from this comes anhartu al-jurh (I widened the wound). The poet said: [Qays ibn al-Khatim, describing a stab wound. Malakt means I strengthened and fortified.]

*I held it with my hand and widened its opening, so that one standing beyond it can see what lies behind it.*

Abu Mijlaz, Abu Nahik, al-A'raj, Talhah ibn Musarrif and Qatadah read (wa-nuhurin) with two dammas, as if it were the plural of nahar (day), meaning they have no night, like sahab and suhub (clouds). Al-Farra' said: some Arabs recited to me:

*If that is my night, then I am a day-person; when I see the dawn, I do not wait.*

That is, the possessor of the day. Another said:

*Were it not for the two thrids, we would have perished with the dried meat: a thrid of night and a thrid of day.*

(In a seat of truth) That is, an assembly of truth, in which there is no idle talk and no sin; and it is Paradise. (In the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful) That is, One who is capable of whatever He wills. Here (ʿinda, "in the presence of") denotes nearness, proximity, station, rank, honour and status. Al-Sadiq said: Allah praised the place of truth, so none sits in it except the people of truth. Uthman al-Batti read (fi maqa'id sidq), in the plural. Al-maqa'id are the places where people sit in markets and elsewhere. Abdullah ibn Buraydah said: the people of Paradise enter every day upon the Mighty, may He be blessed and exalted, and they recite the Qur'an to their Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, each person having sat in his own seat, upon pulpits of pearl, ruby, chrysolite, gold and silver, according to the measure of their deeds. Their eyes are never gladdened by anything as they are gladdened by that, and they have never heard anything greater or finer than it. Then they return to their dwellings, their eyes comforted, to a similar gathering the next day. Thawr ibn Yazid related from Khalid ibn Ma'dan: It has reached us that on the Day of Resurrection the angels will come to the believers and say: "O friends of Allah, set out!" They will ask: "To where?" They will say: "To Paradise." The believers will say: "You are taking us to other than our desire." They will say: "What is your desire?" They will say: "A seat of truth in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful."

This report has also been transmitted specifically with this meaning: it is said that a group of those who were wise regarding Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be escorted by the angels to Paradise while people are still being reckoned. They will say to the angels: "To where are you carrying us?" They will say: "To Paradise." They will say: "You are carrying us to other than our desire." They will say: "What is your desire?" They will say: "The seat of truth with the Beloved, as He informed: (in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful)." And Allah knows best.

The commentary on Surah (al-Qamar) is complete, and praise be to Allah.

Their eyes are never gladdened by anything as they are gladdened by that, and they have never heard anything greater or finer than it. Then they return to their dwellings, their eyes comforted, to a similar gathering the next day. Thawr ibn Yazid related from Khalid ibn Ma'dan: It has reached us that on the Day of Resurrection the angels will come to the believers and say: "O friends of Allah, set out!" They will ask: "To where?" They will say: "To Paradise." The believers will say: "You are taking us to other than our desire." They will say: "What is your desire?" They will say: "A seat of truth in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful."

This report has also been transmitted specifically with this meaning: it is said that a group of those who were wise regarding Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be escorted by the angels to Paradise while people are still being reckoned. They will say to the angels: "To where are you carrying us?" They will say: "To Paradise." They will say: "You are carrying us to other than our desire." They will say: "What is your desire?" They will say: "The seat of truth with the Beloved, as He informed: (in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful)." And Allah knows best.

The commentary on Surah (al-Qamar) is complete, and praise be to Allah.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 50–55:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Our command is but one [word], like a glance of the eye.﴾ That is, but a single time, once.

(Like a glance of the eye) That is, My decree concerning My creation is swifter than the glance of the eye. Al-lamh (the glance) is looking quickly. It is said: he glanced at the lightning with his eye (lamaha al-barq bi-basarihi). In al-Sihah (the lexicon of al-Jawhari): lamaha and alamaha mean he saw it with a light look, and the noun is al-lamhah. Lamaha al-barq and al-najm lamhan means it flashed.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed We have destroyed your likes﴾ That is, your counterparts in disbelief from the previous nations. It is also said: your followers and your helpers.

(Then is there any who will remember?) That is, who will take heed. That is, everything the nations before them did, whether good or bad, was written against them. This explains His saying: (Indeed, We have created everything according to a measure).

(In the scriptures) That is, in the Preserved Tablet. It is said: in the records of the angels who record deeds. It is also said: in the Mother of the Book.

(And every small and great matter is recorded) That is, every sin, great or small, is written against its doer before he does it, so that he may be recompensed for it; and it is written once he has done it. Satara yasturu satran means he wrote; and istatara is similar to it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers﴾ Having described the disbelievers, He also described the believers.

(And rivers) meaning rivers of water, wine, honey and milk; this was said by Ibn Jurayj. It is in the singular because it is the end of the verse; and the singular may also indicate the plural. It is also said: in (nahr) there is the meaning of light and expanse; and from this comes al-nahar (the day), for its light. And from this comes anhartu al-jurh (I widened the wound). The poet said: [Qays ibn al-Khatim, describing a stab wound. Malakt means I strengthened and fortified.]

*I held it with my hand and widened its opening, so that one standing beyond it can see what lies behind it.*

Abu Mijlaz, Abu Nahik, al-A'raj, Talhah ibn Musarrif and Qatadah read (wa-nuhurin) with two dammas, as if it were the plural of nahar (day), meaning they have no night, like sahab and suhub (clouds). Al-Farra' said: some Arabs recited to me:

*If that is my night, then I am a day-person; when I see the dawn, I do not wait.*

That is, the possessor of the day. Another said:

*Were it not for the two thrids, we would have perished with the dried meat: a thrid of night and a thrid of day.*

(In a seat of truth) That is, an assembly of truth, in which there is no idle talk and no sin; and it is Paradise. (In the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful) That is, One who is capable of whatever He wills. Here (ʿinda, "in the presence of") denotes nearness, proximity, station, rank, honour and status. Al-Sadiq said: Allah praised the place of truth, so none sits in it except the people of truth. Uthman al-Batti read (fi maqa'id sidq), in the plural.
